title: Isochron sprint — lab notes and mini-bench
content:
Quick summary:
- Purpose: run short, fixed-interval (isochronal) request streams to characterize how small inter-request spacing affects P50/P95/P99 when the KV cache is partially warm and when the runtime switches quantized kernels. The goal was to reproduce the small, repeatable hiccups some product teams saw during steady user sessions.

Environment and harness:
- Cluster: dev-dedicated-a10g-x2 (2x A10G), CUDA 12.2, 64GB RAM per node.
- Runtime build: serving-runtime@main (commit 7f3c21d) with experimental "micro-sched" enabled.
- Model: rdx-2.7B-fp16 (no quantize), and rdx-2.7B-4bit for variant comparisons.
- Ingress: synthetic client that issues N requests at fixed intervals (isochronal spacing) using HTTP/2 streaming client.
- Test harness params: requests=10000, concurrency=16, interval=4ms (isochronal), payload: chat-like prompt, seq_len=512 avg, max=768.
- KV cache priming: three modes: cold (no prior requests), partial-warm (seed set = 30% of unique prefixes), hot (full warm).

Hypothesis going in:
1) Isochronal 4ms spacing will topologically align kernels to create hot-path contention causing small latency spikes at P95/P99 even while p50 stays low.
2) Quantized variant will reduce p50 but increase p99 due to occasional kernel swap/slowpath for certain heads.

Runs and observations (raw-ish):
- Run A: FP16, cold cache, interval 4ms, concurrency 16
  - throughput sustained: ~250 qps
  - p50: 24ms, p95: 82ms, p99: 210ms
  - notes: clear periodic clustering of spikes every ~1.1s (see timeline section). GPU util ~72%, small CPU spikes on host.

- Run B: FP16, partial-warm, interval 4ms, concurrency 16
  - throughput: ~310 qps
  - p50: 18ms, p95: 47ms, p99: 160ms
  - notes: improving tail but p99 still large; KV cache misses correlated with IP mapping eviction events.

- Run C: 4-bit, partial-warm, interval 4ms, concurrency 16
  - throughput: ~420 qps
  - p50: 13ms, p95: 64ms, p99: 320ms
  - notes: lower median but much worse p99 — sporadic slow calls aligning with quantized kernel fallback (observed long compile-like stall in logs). GPU util 85% plus occasional host-side memcpy stalls.

- Run D: FP16, hot-cache, interval 4ms, concurrency 16
  - throughput: ~480 qps
  - p50: 12ms, p95: 28ms, p99: 76ms
  - notes: stable when cache fully warm. Suggests pattern is cache-priming related.

Timeline / trace-pattern (qualitative):
- Every run with partial or cold priming shows micro-clusters of slow requests approximately every 1–1.3s. Traces show multiple concurrent requests contending on the same kernel launch path and then cascading into host-side stalls.
- Flamegraphs hint at a narrow window where a lock around kernel selection + a pagefault-ish memcpy occasionally serializes many goroutines.

Quick root-cause candidates:
1) KV cache eviction pressure + rehydration causing slow cache loads that block request handling paths (esp. code paths that synchronously fetch/initialize KV slices).
2) Kernel selection code path not fully async; quantized kernels may trigger fallback compilation or slower memcpy schedules under pressure.
3) Network ingress shaping with fixed 4ms intervals + concurrency 16 creates microburst alignments that linearly amplify the above two problems.

Small reproduction artifact (how to repro locally):
- Start single-node dev build (serving-runtime debug) with verbose kernel logs
- Run harness: ./isochron-client --target http://localhost:8080 --qps 250 --concurrency 16 --interval-ms 4 --requests 10000 --prefix-seed 30
- Watch /metrics and runtime logs for: kernel-select latency, kv-fetch latencies, host memcpy queuing.

Immediate mitigations to try (cheap experiments):
- Make kernel selection lock-free (fast-path) or batch kernel selection for a small window (50ms) to avoid per-request serialization.
- Prefetch KV slices asynchronously when cold/partial; convert the synchronous cold-path into an async fill + best-effort fallback.
- Add micro-jitter to ingress client (random +/- 1ms) — confirm if removing strict isochron reduces alignment effect. (Already tried: adding jitter +-1.5ms reduced p99 by ~30% in FP16 partial-warm run.)
- For quantized variant: ensure no compile-ish operation occurs at runtime; pre-warm kernel caches at startup.

Evaluation notes (what mattered most):
- Warmth of KV cache is dominant factor for p99 under isochronal spacing. Hot-cache runs are much cleaner.
- Quantization improves raw throughput and p50 but is fragile unless kernel/host paths are pre-initialized.
- Small ingress jitter is a cheap and effective mitigation but not a long-term solution — better to fix serialization points.

Action items / next steps:
- [ ] Create ENG-INF ticket to add async KV prefetch + break sync cold-path (owner: Ravi). (ENG-INF-4821 linked.)
- [ ] Instrument kernel selection with higher sampling frequency and add telemetry dimensions for "kernel-selection-latency" (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Run controlled jitter experiments across wider ranges (+-0.5ms, +-1ms, +-2ms) to quantify tradeoffs and update docs for recommended client spacing for PLG customers. (Assign: me)
- [ ] Add a pre-warm step for quantized variants in deployment test harness (PR drafted: linked).

Notes to future-me: keep an eye on host memcpy queue length — it correlates strongly with the p99 spikes. Save the heavy trace from run C (TS:2026-02-28 19:44) and attach to PR.

Raw sample timeline excerpt (from one trace, human-readable):
[t=0.000] req 1232 start
[t=0.012] req 1233 start
[t=0.016] req 1234 start
[t=0.026] kernel-select lock acquired (req 1232)
[t=0.026] reqs 1233/1234 blocked waiting on kernel-select
[t=0.040] req 1232 kernel memcpy -> host 1.8ms
[t=0.044] req 1233 resume -> schedule kernel
[t=0.300] long exit path observed (req 1232) -> p99 contributor

Attachments to add: trace JSON (run-C-2026-02-28.json), perf flamegraph (runC-flame.svg), short client script (isochron-client.sh).

Bottom line (for product owners):
- If your app experiences intermittent spikes at P99 even with low median latency, ask whether your traffic has very regular intervals or if it uses small, repeated prefixes that cause partial cache warm conditions. These two conditions together are a likely root cause.

Freeform thoughts / brainstorming:
- Could we expose a "recommended client jitter" knob in the SDK? Documented as "reduces aligned microbursts" — quick win for customers who cannot change server internals.
- Consider a small background kernel prefetcher that opportunistically touches quantized kernels during low-load windows.

End of notes.
